text: MEASURE N TOWN ATTORNEY'S IMPARTIAL ANALYSIS .7
The Portola Valley Town Council placed Measure N on the ballot to ask Portola Valley voters to 1 3 approve both a Town Charter and a tax on the sale of real property ("RPTT"). 15

California law recognizes two types of towns—general law towns and charter towns. Portola Yall*' is currently a general law town with powers granted to it by the California Constitution and other state laws. Its acts must be consistent with state law. IZ

In contrast, the California Constitution authorizes charter towns and cities to adopt local rules 14 regarding "municipal affairs" that are different from state law, sometimes called "home rule" 13 authority. A charter town's charter explains which municipal affairs are within the town's home 14 rule authority. Charter towns must still comply with state law regarding matters of "statewide 14 concern. "

The proposed Portola Valley Charter ("Charter") would make a charter town and I a authorize the Town Council to exercise home rule authority over municipal affairs relating to 14 local taxes, including the RPTT. The Charter itself would not change existing local laws, like the Municipal Code. The Town would otherwise be subject to and governed by the general laws of I e the State, unless the voters amended the Charter. 9

Measure N would also authorize the Town to enact an RPTT that exceeds the rate authorized by 17 state law for general law towns. The Town currently imposes a tax on the transfer of real property at the rate of twenty-seven and one-half cents ($0.275) per five-hundred dollars ($500) 14 of the sales price of property, which is the maximum tax rate permitted under state law for ( 7 general law towns. Charter towns may increase the RPTT tax rate. II

Measure N would authorize the Town to levy the RPTT at the rate often dollars ($10) per one 1 q thousand dollars ($1 ,000) of consideration paid for real property. The RPTT only applies to the 15 transfer of real property for consideration. For example, the RPTT would generally not apply to 16 property that is solely transferred by inheritance. In addition, the RPTT would not apply to 15 transactions that qualify under one of the enumerated exemptions. The buyer and seller can 14 negotiate responsibility for payment of the RPTT. 7

The Measure authorizes the Town Council to reduce or eliminate the RPTT rate and to provide 16 additional exemptions without a vote of the people, but it does not permit the Town Council to 17 raise the RPTT above the authorized rate without additional voter approval. II

The RPTT would be a general tax because the revenue would be deposited into the Town's I V general fund and could be used for any legitimate Town purpose. If approved, the Measure 16 would generate approximately $2 million of additional revenue annually. q

A "Yes" vote is a vote to adopt the Charter and authorize the RPTT. A "No" vote is a vote against 21 the Charter and RPTT. Measure N would be approved if it received a simple majority of "Yes" 17 votes.
Catherine Engberg 2 Town Attorney, Town of Portola Valley ] end 3

text: Reports of the Town's imminent financial demise or invasion are greatly exaggerated! 12-
Proponents' fear-mongering is fantasy, and only highlights their absence of a defense for the flawed property transfer tax itself.
We are not at risk of financial collapse or loss of self-determination. Disincorporation in 14 California last happened in 1973, for a single Southern California town.

Town finance staff's budget projections cover all expenses, including continuing public safety 12 and wildfire mitigation/protection funding through end of FY 2028 before approaching our 20% 3 cash reserves. Even with no new taxes, there are two additional years before reserves are 16 depleted in FY2030. 8
Council could have offered a second, alternative tax measure, broadly equitable, in this 13 election, for voters to choose between.
A modest parcel or utility user's tax increase of $800 or less per residence per year could spread 8 the tax burden equitably across virtually all residents.

Or a fairer transfer tax, applied on the difference between sale price and current tas.:.assess— 15 value, with an exemption for sellers or buyers who have paid another transfer tax recently ona replacement property. 2

Remember: Council asked their own Finance Committee to research alternative tax measures 12 and provisions, but DIDN'T ASK FOR OR RECEIVE either a recommendation or endorsement 13 far this confiscatory transfer tax. WHY?
We should strive to share taxes fairly for the kind of Town we all want—not to saddle a ( q huge exit toll on our departing neighbors.
Send Council back with a NO vote. There's still time to get this right. / end 14

text: REBUTTAL TO ARGUMENT AGAINST MEASURE "N"
We must act immediately to raise additional revenues.

Yes on "N" Protects Portola Valley's Financial Stability and Independence. We PO must act now to ensure our Town's long-term financial viability and avoid losing our 14 status as a locally controlled/incorporated Town. If we don't, we'll be forced to severely 15 cut service levels and become unable to fund critical local needs such as emergency preparedness, wildfire prevention and maintaining our infrastructure. 7

Yes on "N" Offers an Effective, Near-Term Solution. After extensive analysis (including significant input by the Finance Committee), a local Real Property Transfer Tax (RPTT) was selected as the best solution. To enact it, the Town must become a Charter Town. This will be straightforward, mirroring closely our current administrative structure and practices.

Yes on "N" Adopts a Known Path for Raising Revenues. Many cities in the Bay 16 Area have enacted similar RPTT measures to address severe budget challenges. 11 RPTTs apply only when a property is sold . The major alternative considered, a parcel tax, is harder to enact and regressive: imposed on each parcel, each year, forcing homeowners to suffer an increased annual tax burden no matter what their circumstances.

Under Measure N, local revenues will be locally controlled. Homeowners will have the benefit of currently applicable county RPTT exemptions. In implementing Measure N, the Town may create additional exemptions, and may consider additional measures to enhance accountability to residents for use of these revenueså
Doing nothing is not an option. IO Vote YES on N - protect the future of our Town. end
